title: Conservative Continuous-Time Treatment Optimization
claim: Conservative regularization yields predictions that track true responses and lowers ground-truth cost relative to naive optimization across tasks.
layout: 3 panel groups: top trajectory line plots, bottom two boxplot rows; shared legends
description: Figure with three parts. Panel A (top) has three line plots on the Covid-19 task. The left plot shows an optimized treatment trajectory over time. Thick tan, pink and blue lines mark different regularization strengths, a dotted black line marks the optimal plan, and thin gray lines show training plans. The middle and right plots show lung-tissue dexamethasone concentration. Gray true curves are overlaid with predicted curves. With λ=0 the tan predictions miss the true peak. With λ=1000 the blue predictions match it. Panels B and C (bottom) are rows of boxplots of relative ground-truth cost for Cancer-Explicit, Cancer-Relative and COVID-19. B varies λ and C varies the number of intervals K. A dotted line at 1 marks naive optimization. Colored boxes drop below it as regularization increases.
caption: \ours on PK/PD tasks. A.: Optimized treatment plans (left) and corresponding predicted and true states (right). B. & C.: Relative ground-truth cost for different $\lambda\in\{1,10,100,1000\}$ with $K=1$, and $K \in \{1,2,4,6\}$ with $\lambda=10$ using a linear kernel. Values below 1 indicate improvement over naive optimization. Boxplots show medians and IQRs, with whiskers extending to the most extreme points within $1.5$ IQRs over 15 optimization task initializations.
abstract: Finding optimal treatment plans in continuous time is crucial for personalized medicine. Existing methods, however, do not explicitly optimize treatment plans and instead focus solely on predicting treatment effects. Naive optimization over these treatment-response models can exploit model errors, resulting in plans that appear optimal under the learned model but perform poorly in practice. To mitigate model exploitation, we propose SigCTO (Signature-based Conservative Treatment Optimization), a conservative framework for continuous-time treatment optimization. We derive a path-space regularizer based on signature-kernel maximum mean discrepancy that penalizes treatment plans for which predicted and true responses differ. Under suitable assumptions, the regularizer allows for consistent estimation, and the regularized objective upper bounds the true treatment cost. Experiments on pharmacometric simulators show that SigCTO finds treatment plans with lower ground-truth costs than state-of-the-art baselines. On real-world ICU data, SigCTO predicts treatment cost more accurately than baselines, and the regularizer detects prediction errors.
